themes.label: Introduction: generalization error and CV variance estimation
themes.need: Someone wanting to perform statistical inference (a test or confidence interval) on an algorithm's generalization error needs the definition of generalization error, the review of existing cross-validation-based estimators, and the motivation for a more careful treatment of their variance.

themes.label: Analysis of Var[mu_J]
themes.need: Someone wanting the exact variance of the J-replicate cross-validation mean estimator needs Lemmas 1-2 and Propositions 1-3 characterizing Var[mu_J] in terms of the correlation between replicate estimates, laying the theoretical foundation for the variance-estimation methods that follow.

themes.label: Estimating Var[mu_J]: approximating rho (first method)
themes.need: Someone wanting a practical variance estimator for the cross-validation mean needs the first proposed method, which approximates the unknown inter-replicate correlation rho by a simple closed-form surrogate.

themes.label: Estimating Var[mu_J]: conservative overestimate (second method)
themes.need: Someone wanting a variance estimator that errs on the safe (conservative) side rather than approximating the unknown correlation needs the second proposed method, which deliberately overestimates Var[mu_J].

themes.label: Seven techniques for inference about mu
themes.need: Someone choosing among competing methods to build a hypothesis test or confidence interval for the generalization error needs the catalog of seven techniques (t-test/McNemar, resampled t, Dietterich's 5x2cv, conservative Z, pseudo-bootstrap, corrected resampled t, corrected pseudo-bootstrap), their estimator/statistic definitions, and the 'political ratio' analysis of whether each is liberal or conservative.

themes.label: Simulation study design and setup
themes.need: Someone wanting to empirically compare the seven inference techniques needs the simulation study's data-generating design and experimental setup used to measure their size and power.

themes.label: Sizes and powers of tests: simulation results
themes.need: Someone deciding which inference technique to trust in practice needs the simulation results comparing the empirical size (type-I error) and power of the seven techniques.

themes.label: Choice of J: simulation guidance
themes.need: Someone implementing a J-replicate cross-validation inference procedure needs the simulation-based guidance on how to choose J (the number of resampling replicates) for good size/power tradeoffs.

themes.label: Choice of M: simulation guidance
themes.need: Someone using the conservative-Z method needs the simulation-based guidance on how to choose M, the parameter controlling that method's degree of conservativeness.

themes.label: Appendix A: statistical prerequisites
themes.need: Someone wanting to follow the paper's proofs needs Appendix A's statistical prerequisites (background definitions and results) assumed by the subsequent proofs.

themes.label: Proof of Lemma 2
themes.need: Someone wanting to verify the distributional result used to justify the corrected resampled-t and pseudo-bootstrap statistics needs the full proof of Lemma 2.

themes.label: Proof of Proposition 2
themes.need: Someone wanting to verify one of the variance-structure propositions from Section 2 needs the full proof of Proposition 2.

themes.label: Inference when vectors have moments as in Lemma 1
themes.need: Someone wanting inference results under the more general moment conditions of Lemma 1 (rather than the idealized Gaussian/equal-rho case) needs this extension of the inference theory to that setting.

themes.label: Numbered explanatory notes
themes.need: Someone wanting the detailed footnote-level clarifications referenced throughout the paper (by numbered superscript) needs this consolidated notes section.
